title: NABL Accreditation Process
shortDescription: The general journey a laboratory goes through to become — and stay — NABL accredited, from choosing a programme to ongoing surveillance.
genZNote: Accreditation isn't a certificate you get once. It's a status you keep proving.

sections.heading: The Accreditation Journey
sections.body: While exact timelines, fees, and document formats can change over time and are set by NABL's current official procedures (never memorise a fixed number here — always check NABL's current guidance), the GENERAL shape of the journey is stable and exam-relevant.

steps.name: Select the applicable accreditation programme
steps.explanation: The lab identifies which programme fits its work — testing, calibration, medical, PT provider, RMP, or biobank.
steps.purpose: Different programmes assess against different standards (ISO/IEC 17025 vs ISO 15189, etc.).

steps.name: Define scope
steps.explanation: The lab specifies exactly which tests/calibrations/examinations it wants accredited — accreditation is never granted as a blanket approval.
steps.purpose: Assessors only evaluate competence for what's actually declared in scope.

steps.name: Application and document review
steps.explanation: The lab submits its application along with quality manual/SOPs; NABL reviews these documents before any on-site visit.
steps.purpose: Catches major gaps before committing assessor time to an on-site visit.

steps.name: Assessment
steps.explanation: A team of NABL-appointed technical assessors evaluates the lab on-site (or through applicable assessment stages) against the standard, for the declared scope.
steps.purpose: This is the core technical competence check.

steps.name: Nonconformities, if identified
steps.explanation: Any gap between what the lab does and what the standard requires is raised as a nonconformity.
steps.purpose: Nonconformities aren't a failure state — they're the normal mechanism for identifying gaps.

steps.name: Corrective action
steps.explanation: The lab investigates the root cause of each nonconformity and implements and evidences a fix.
steps.purpose: Accreditation isn't withheld for having gaps; it's withheld for not fixing them.

steps.name: Decision
steps.explanation: NABL's accreditation decision-making process reviews the assessment findings and corrective actions to decide on granting accreditation.
steps.purpose: Kept independent from the assessment team itself, for impartiality.

steps.name: Accreditation
steps.explanation: The lab is granted accreditation for its defined scope, valid for a defined period.
steps.purpose: This is a STATUS, not a one-time award — it must be actively maintained.

steps.name: Surveillance / reassessment
steps.explanation: Ongoing periodic checks (surveillance) and full reassessment before the accreditation period ends, per NABL's applicable current requirements.
steps.purpose: Confirms competence is maintained, not just present on assessment day.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: NABL accreditation follows a general journey — programme selection, scope definition, application, assessment, correction of any nonconformities, a decision, and then ongoing surveillance/reassessment — with exact timelines and fees set by NABL's current official procedures.
keyFacts: Scope is defined by the laboratory BEFORE assessment, and assessors evaluate only against that declared scope.
Nonconformities are a normal, expected part of the process — not an automatic failure.
The accreditation decision is kept separate from the assessment team, for impartiality.
Accreditation must be actively maintained through surveillance and periodic reassessment — it is not permanent.

highYieldFacts: The general accreditation journey is stable across programmes even though exact timelines/fees change over time — never memorise a fixed number.
Accreditation is a maintained STATUS via surveillance and reassessment, not a one-time certificate.
commonTraps: Assuming a nonconformity automatically means accreditation is refused — it triggers corrective action, not automatic failure.
mustRemember: Order: Programme selection → Scope → Application/document review → Assessment → Nonconformities/corrective action → Decision → Accreditation → Surveillance/reassessment.
possibleQuestions: Outline the general stages of the NABL accreditation process for a new applicant laboratory.

sources.name: NABL — National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories

questions.prompt: In the NABL accreditation process, WHO makes the final accreditation decision?
options: The same assessors who conducted the on-site assessment
A separate decision-making process, kept independent of the assessment team
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry directly
questions.explanation: Keeping the decision separate from the assessment team preserves impartiality.

questions.prompt: True or False: A nonconformity found during assessment automatically means the laboratory is denied accreditation.
questions.explanation: Nonconformities trigger corrective action, not automatic denial — they're a normal, expected part of the process.
